MacPaw announces a long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to jointly develop an on-device AI technology stack tailored for Mac.

The collaboration will begin with Eney, MacPaw's AI assistant for macOS.

MacPaw partners with Liquid AI to bring more on-device AI capabilities to Mac

Liquid AI's Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be adapted for Mac-based assistance features, and combined with MacPaw's proprietary on-device technologies: Mnemos for memory and Elix for inference.

Eney already switched to local models last year, keeping reasoning, context search, skill execution, and conversation history on-device as much as possible.

This new partnership aims to push that direction further. The two companies will co-develop the underlying technology stack, rather than MacPaw simply plugging in another third-party model.

MacPaw says once the technology is tested and deployed on Eney, it plans to roll it out to more of the company's products. They also hope to open up the shared AI technology stack to Mac developers through Setapp.

Doing so would let participating apps expose more of their own features and contextual information to Eney, enabling the assistant to understand the app's internals and provide more useful answers or perform relevant actions.
